# equipe

> equipe is a startup team for one person: AI agents in the roles of a PM, engineers, a designer, QA and a data analyst take an idea, or something the person already built in Claude or a similar tool, live as a real service (hosting, database, domain), watch how people use it and propose the next improvement. The person approves anything that goes live, costs money or reaches customers. It runs in the cloud and is used in the browser (app.equipe.im); no Mac or code is needed. Sign-up is open: start at https://app.equipe.im/start (add ?idea=<text> to bring an idea along); returning users sign in at https://app.equipe.im/login. Pricing: 100 credits = $1 (the product shows credits, not dollars); credit packs of $25 (2,500 credits), $50, $100 and $250, plus $990 for 110,000 credits, valid 12 months, unused credits refundable within 14 days. Free start: 500 credits when the team is created (1,000 more when a card is added, no charge); no card needed. One paid plan, the Team plan: hosting, storage, 5 people and a monthly amount of credits the person chooses; the price is the total: {{m0}}/month with no credits (keeps the product live), {{m1}} with {{c1}} credits, {{m2}} with {{c2}} (where most teams start), {{m3}} with {{c3}}, {{m4}} with {{c4}}; yearly applies to the base fee only ({{fromYear}}/year instead of {{m0}}/month, 2 months free; the chosen credits stay monthly at 100 credits = $1 and roll over 3 months); plan credits are used at 100 credits = $1 and roll over for 2 months; each extra editor $5/month, up to 10 per team; view-only invites free; credits are shared by the whole team; Free includes 2 people. Everything the team does while it works is paid from credits: AI work at the model's list price plus margin (shown to the cent per task) and the cloud computer it works on; when the team is not working it costs nothing. A team stops only when credits run out; adding credits lets it continue right away. Every request shows its expected cost first, and the user sets a monthly cap. Weekly growth reports are live: the person picks the day and time, and the report carries growth suggestions they approve with one tap. Not shipped yet: one-step import from Claude with a database and domain.

## What the team delivers from the first launch

Every product the team puts live comes with, with no setup by the person: a live site on its own address (plus three custom domain suggestions: best, best value, cheapest; a domain is bought only after the person approves its yearly price; the domain and the team's work are paid from credits, and nothing on this list carries a separate fee); a privacy policy and terms written from the features the product really uses, with booking, minors or health clauses when they apply; a contact page that mails the owner; search and AI visibility (a title and description on every page, sitemap, structured data, share images, llms.txt, IndexNow pings on every deploy, and guided Google Search Console and Bing setup); share-ready posts per platform, Instagram story and post images and one-tap sharing; marketing tools (Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, Google Ads, TikTok, LinkedIn) that load only after a visitor accepts the cookie banner; sign-up source tracking, a feedback widget and a one-time "how did you hear about us" question; an admin area for products with sign-in; speed measured on a phone after every release (target 95 or more, a fix is scheduled automatically when it drops); uptime monitoring; a measured before and after when an existing site is improved; and a weekly growth report on the day and time the person picks. Details: https://equipe.im/day-one/

## AI in your product

Products built with equipe can use AI without an AI account or an API key. The person tells their equipe team what they want, such as a chatbot that answers questions about their prices, and the team adds it from 11 ready-made features: on the site, a support chatbot, instant FAQ answers, site translation, smart form fill and recommendations; in the admin, review and booking summaries, product descriptions, reply drafts and images for posts; behind the scenes, inquiry triage (hot, warm, cold) and comment and review checks. Usage is paid from the team's equipe credits at the AI provider's list price plus 10%, with no separate AI subscription. Every product has a monthly AI limit (1,000 credits unless the person changes it), a note at 80% and a friendly pause at the limit, plus limits per product, per signed-in user and per visitor. Each product gets its own key kept on its server (equipe stores only a hash), calls from a browser are refused, the assistant's instructions stay on equipe's side, and equipe does not store prompts or answers, only counts and costs; the AI provider receives each message to answer it. Not available yet: voice to text, a ready-made component for reading photos, search by meaning across a whole site. Developers get an OpenAI-compatible API at https://ai.equipe.im/v1 (chat with streaming, embeddings, images; tiers fast, smart and best). Details: https://equipe.im/features/ai/ · Docs: https://ai.equipe.im/docs

## The open-source engine (for developers)

The team runs on the open-source equipe engine, which developers can run themselves: https://equipe.im/developers/

> The engine is an open-source AI software squad: a team of role-based agents (PM, Designer, Frontend, Backend, Mobile, QA and Data) that works on your repository through a shared board, in isolated git worktrees, and waits for a person's approval before anything merges. It is the team layer on top of existing agent engines (Codex and Claude Code today), not another agent loop. Early-stage, MIT licensed.

## How it works

- Roles: each member has a role with a model suited to it and its own memory.
- Tickets: the board is the single source of truth; members coordinate through tickets and immutable events, not chat.
- Branches: each member works in its own git worktree on its own branch, so several can work at once without touching your checkout.
- Your approval: nothing merges until the person leading the squad says so.
- Projects: one squad works on several projects; the conversation follows the project you pick.
- Decisions: permission requests and the questions members ask arrive as cards you answer with one key or click.
- Desktop app (macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel): released. A signed, notarized DMG from the latest GitHub release that updates itself, in eight languages: a sidebar of live work, a ticket screen (list and board), ⌘K search, a browser panel for the Chrome the members use, phone pairing, and connection to a squad on another Mac over SSH. It needs the `equipe` CLI.
- iPhone app "equipe — AI squad": released, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/equipe-ai-squad/id6822702958. Approve with Face ID. Android app: in preparation, not released yet. Pair with `equipe pair` (QR code); push notifications; messages sealed end to end through a relay. Telegram works today through `equipe telegram setup`.

## Get started

Desktop app (the easiest way, macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel, signed and notarized): download https://github.com/equipe-labs/equipe/releases/latest/download/equipe.dmg, open it and drag equipe to Applications. The app needs the `equipe` CLI and shows how to install it if it is missing; if it says the squad is off, run `equipe` in a terminal.

CLI (macOS and Linux, for the terminal and for the app):

Install a prebuilt `equipe` (it goes in `~/.local/bin`, checked against its SHA-256):

    curl -fsSL https://github.com/equipe-labs/equipe/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

Or with Homebrew:

    brew install equipe-labs/tap/equipe

To build from source instead you need Rust 1.88+ and git (the Claude engine also needs the `claude` binary):

    git clone https://github.com/equipe-labs/equipe && cd equipe
    cargo install --locked --path crates/cli

Then:

    equipe login     # sign in to Codex or Claude Code
    equipe status    # check engine readiness and model availability
    equipe           # open the squad console

## How the team works

Every piece of work runs through a sprint loop: plan (the PM turns the goal into a sprint), build (engineers and designer), ship (QA checks, the person approves going live), measure (the data analyst looks at real usage), retro (what worked and what did not), next sprint. QA, security and maintenance are part of every sprint. The team keeps notes on the product, its users and the person's preferences, and what it measures and learns in retros feeds the next plan.
